title: Macdonald principal specialization ratios and their generating polynomials
summary: We establish independence of $q$ as a necessary condition for coefficientwise nonnegativity of normalized principal specialization ratios of monic Macdonald polynomials. For arbitrary pairs of partitions, we characterize independence of $q$. For denominator partitions with largest and smallest parts differing by at least two, every ratio independent of $q$ is a power of $t$. We classify the nonnegative ratios under addition of maximal rows and columns of fixed height. For rows of length at least two, the classification is equivalent to rectangular complementation.
